components.css: :host{--ground:#ffffff;--ink:#111111;--ink-2:#4a4a4a;--rule:#d6d6d6;--band:#111111;--band-ink:#ffffff;--band-ink-2:#bdbdbd;--hover:#f3f3f3;--focus:#0039a6;--l1:#ee352e;--l2:#f96016;--l3:#fccc0a;--l4:#00933c;--l5:#0039a6;--l6:#b933ad;--l0:#808183;--sans:"Heros","Helvetica Neue",Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;} .ds-bullet{display:inline-grid;place-items:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--c,#808183);color:var(--fg,#fff);font:700 18px/1 var(--sans);letter-spacing:-0.02em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;flex:none;} .ds-bullet.sm{width:22px;height:22px;font-size:11px;} .ds-c1{--c:#ee352e;} .ds-c2{--c:#f96016;} .ds-c3{--c:#fccc0a;--fg:#111;} .ds-c4{--c:#00933c;} .ds-c5{--c:#0039a6;} .ds-c6{--c:#b933ad;} .ds-c0{--c:#808183;} .ds-today{background:var(--band);color:var(--band-ink);position:relative;padding:30px 24px 24px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto auto 1fr;gap:6px 20px;align-items:center;font-family:var(--sans);} .ds-today::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:8px;height:2px;background:var(--band-ink);} .ds-where{font-weight:700;font-size:clamp(26px,4vw,40px);letter-spacing:-0.02em;} .ds-today h2{margin:0;font-size:clamp(22px,3vw,32px);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-0.02em;} .ds-meta{font-size:14px;color:var(--band-ink-2);margin-top:4px;} .ds-acts{grid-column:3;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;margin-top:10px;} .ds-go,.ds-again{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;height:38px;padding:0 14px;font:700 14px var(--sans);text-decoration:none;cursor:pointer;border-radius:0;} .ds-go{background:var(--band-ink);color:#111;} .ds-again{background:transparent;color:var(--band-ink);border:1.5px solid var(--band-ink);} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.ds-today{animation:ds-arrive 420ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} @keyframes ds-arrive{from{clip-path:inset(0 100% 0 0);}to{clip-path:inset(0 0 0 0);}}} :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus,#0039a6);outline-offset:2px;}

components.name: Signage Band
components.description: Full-bleed black masthead/footer band with a 2px white rule 10px below the top edge.
components.html:
New Yorker Fiction, Shortest First

All 7,223 short stories since 1940, ranked by reading time.

An independent index, not affiliated with The New Yorker.

narrative.overview:
The system is the 1970 New York subway signage standard and the 1972 diagram, applied to a reading list. Story length is the train line: every story is a stop led by a colored route bullet carrying its reading time in minutes, and the color tells you which band of time you are riding before you read a word. Black signage bands frame the page top and bottom, each with a thin white rule just inside its top edge; between them sits a white ground of dense rows divided by hairline rules.

It is a light, flat, single-typeface world. One grotesque (TeX Gyre Heros, a license-free Helvetica clone) in two weights does all the work, and scale contrast, not color or decoration, carries the hierarchy. There are no cards, no shadows, no gradients for tone, and no rounded corners: shapes are either square or perfect circles. Color is spent almost entirely on the route bullets, where it encodes data.

The site is light-only by contract. `color-scheme: light` is declared and no dark theme exists; adding one needs the owner's approval.
keyCharacteristics: Route bullets in MTA line colors, keyed to reading time at 240 words a minute.
Black signage bands with a white top rule; one black panel inside the list (Today).
One grotesque, Regular and Bold only, with tabular lining figures for every count.
Dense, card-less rows on white with 1px rules; transfer signs drawn as rules.
Flat everywhere; circles are the only curve.

rules.name: The Line Means Length Rule
rules.body: A line color appears only as a route bullet and only to state a reading-time band. Never use a line color for decoration, emphasis, links or backgrounds. Bands are fixed: under 5, 5–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–45, 45+ minutes, grey for unknown.

rules.name: The One Black Panel Rule
rules.body: Black fills only the masthead band, the footer band, and, inside the list, the Today panel. No other element in the list gets a black panel.

rules.name: The Numeral Color Rule
rules.body: Bullet numerals are white, except on Broadway Yellow, where they are black.

rules.name: The One Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Heros Regular and Bold only. No second family, no italics, no other weights.

rules.name: The Scale Does Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Rank is shown by size and the Regular/Bold switch, never by color. Text color is black, Station Grey, or their on-black equivalents.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every count, word total, minute and word span sets in tabular lining figures so columns of numbers hold still.

rules.name: The Flat Signage Rule
rules.body: No box shadows, no blur, no tonal gradients. If something must stand forward, it turns black or gets a heavier rule.

rules.name: The Circle-or-Square Rule
rules.body: A shape is either square-cornered or a perfect circle. No intermediate radii, pills or rounded rectangles.

dos: Do lead every story with a route bullet in its band's line color, minutes inside, computed at 240 words a minute.
Do keep text to Heros Regular (400) and Bold (700), and use Bold where the signage tradition uses Medium.
Do set every number in tabular lining figures.
Do separate rows with 1px Hairline Grey (#d6d6d6) rules and draw line headers as rules (5px over, 1px under), not panels.
Do put the thin white rule inside the top edge of every black band or panel (2px).
Do use 1.5px black borders and square corners on all controls, and the 2px Signal Blue outline for focus.
donts: Don't use a line color for anything except a reading-time bullet.
Don't add a second black panel inside the list; Today is the only one.
Don't use cards, shadows, tonal gradients, or any radius other than a perfect circle.
Don't add a second typeface, italics or intermediate weights, or serve the magazine's proprietary fonts.
Don't add a dark theme without the owner's approval; the world is light-only.
Don't rank text with line colors or extra grey tints; size and weight do that, with Station Grey reserved for secondary text.
